sources.title: A. Nichols, The Temperley-Lieb algebra and its generalizations in the Potts and XXZ models
sources.locator: Complete 51-page PDF fetched and inspected at §2, especially the Temperley-Lieb presentation and §§2.1.2–2.1.4, equations (2.1), (2.2), (2.4), (2.6)–(2.10): Q=2,3,4 open Potts clock/shift matrices, loop weights, selected q values and the uniform free-boundary Hamiltonian.

contents.name: §2.1.2–2.1.4, equations (2.4), (2.6)–(2.10): explicit open Q-state Potts generators and q values
contents.support: Confirms the exact finite clock/shift conventions and the open-endpoint range. The weighted real-coupling matrix and Hermiticity are defined and proved locally; no integrability claim is imported.

contents.name: §2, equation (2.1) and §2.2, equation (2.2): loop delta and the uniform free-boundary TL Hamiltonian
contents.support: Supplies an independent Potts-chain treatment with the same delta=sqrt(Q) normalization and identifies only the uniform open-chain Hamiltonian. The local proof establishes all representation and Hecke relations directly.

contents.name: §2.1.2–2.1.4: local projector realization for two sites
contents.support: Supports the finite two-site clock/shift setup. The projector overlap, noncommutation, and non-diagonal Gibbs conclusion are proved in the local example.

contents.name: Representation-theoretic spectrum matching and later boundary, periodic, or scaling material outside §2.1
contents.support: No XXZ spectral matching, boundary extension, scaling limit, phase transition, or thermodynamic assertion is made in this batch.
contents.reason: These results are outside the four finite-dimensional local algebra and matrix claims.

sources.title: David Penneys, Exercises in quantum algebra
sources.locator: Complete 66-page graduate course-note PDF fetched; Chapter 2 §§2.1.1–2.1.3, PDF pp. 5–8: algebraic generators, diagram multiplication with loop factor d, diagram generators E_i, and the normalization map from algebraic to diagrammatic TL.

contents.name: Chapter 2, §§2.1.1–2.1.3: abstract and diagrammatic Temperley-Lieb normalizations
contents.support: Independent full-course-note treatment confirms the loop weight and the distinction between idempotently rescaled algebraic generators and unnormalized diagram generators whose square contributes d.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §2.1.2: cap/cup generators, stacking direction, loop scalar
contents.support: Supports the diagram convention stated with the TikZ TL generator. The proof does not rely on the diagram.

contents.name: Later Jones-Wenzl, trace, tower and category material
contents.support: No tower, trace-radical, semisimplicity, or categorical statement is claimed here.
contents.reason: The assigned items use only the local TL relations and finite matrix representation.

sources.locator: Complete 71-page PDF fetched; §2.1 Type A, Definition 1, PDF pp. 3–4, equation (2.1), with the stated q nonzero condition and the q=1 specialization.

contents.name: §2.1 Type A, Definition 1, equation (2.1): (g_i-q)(g_i+q^{-1})=0, braid and distant commutation
contents.support: Confirms the Hecke normalization used by the local generators. The source’s generic semisimplicity condition is not used.

contents.name: The generic semisimplicity condition and later qKZ solution results
contents.support: The Potts q values at Q=2,3 are roots of unity, and this batch makes no Hecke semisimplicity, qKZ, Bethe, or completeness assertion.
contents.reason: These claims are not needed for the elementary local relation proof.

sources.title: Yacine Ikhlef, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, and Hubert Saleur, A Temperley-Lieb quantum chain with two- and three-site interactions
sources.locator: Complete 9-page paper fetched; Introduction and §2, PDF pp. 1–4, especially equation (2) for the TL relations and the spin-1/2 projector realization at q=1.

contents.name: Introduction and §2: loop-weight-two spin-half representation and singlet projector normalization
contents.support: Confirms that at q=1 the spin-half TL generator is twice the adjacent singlet projection. The local theorem uses the current NRQM carrier and proves the exchange identity algebraically.

contents.name: Two- and three-site interaction phase diagram, Bethe solution and spectral claims
contents.support: No phase diagram, gap, integrability, or thermodynamic-limit conclusion is transferred.
contents.reason: The assigned statement is a finite algebraic identity.

sources.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §7.4 Variational Density Matrix Method
sources.locator: Full §7.4 page fetched and inspected at “The variational principle” and the finite Ising density-matrix discussion, lines 1352–1414: normalized density matrices, finite-energy Boltzmann weights, and the partition-function normalization.

contents.name: §7.4, variational principle: normalized finite Boltzmann distribution and positive weights
contents.support: Provides an independent statistical-mechanics convention for finite normalized Boltzmann weights. It does not prove the noncommuting matrix case; the local spectral argument establishes self-adjointness, positivity, and finite positive trace.

contents.name: The Ising-specific diagonal ansatz and mean-field minimization
contents.support: No classical Ising diagonal ansatz or mean-field approximation is applied to the noncommuting quantum Potts matrix.
contents.reason: The assigned lemma concerns exact finite-dimensional spectral calculus.
